Steam Market Mayhem Update: Requesting a refund for a mod gets you a 7 day Steam Market ban.

It's really interesting to watch companies like this take such big turns. This is probably the biggest blow to Steam's reputation and customer confidence since back in the days when everyone hated Steam with all of their hearts.

To see a company go from hated, to beloved, all the way back to vilified, really is eye-opening. People who have come to think of this company as some kind of benevolent force showering them with ridiculous discounts are starting to see the bigger picture. Steam is nothing more than another company with dollar signs in their eyes. They saw a way to start a whole new chain of revenue and they took it knowing full well there would be backlash. Just like every other gaming fiasco, they're banking on the fact that gamers as a whole are usually pretty un-unified and pretty easy to distract (you've probably seen the MW2 boycott picture). Look how big of a deal the whole Sim City thing was when it happened, but merely a few weeks later people just stopped caring and many of those who swore boycotts against EA were making plans for their next pre-order. As much of an uproar as this is causing, we also have to remember that those who are shouting against it are the vocal minority. For every person who is filled with rage at this obvious cash grab, there are six people who either haven't heard a word about it or don't give a rat's ass, they just like to play video games.

This will come and this will go and six months from now nobody will care. This will surely be a stain on Steam/Valve's reputation and it's bound to cost them some loyal customers, but I am in no way convinced we will see any positives come from this situation and I can almost assure you the money they make from complacent customers will more than offset the money lost by fucking us all collectively.

If you have issued a refund on your Steam account to your Wallet, you will be restricted from using the Market for 7 days while the funds are verified.
